summary: Vinnytsia/Gavyryshivka International Airport (VIN) is a medium-sized regional airport serving the city of Vinnytsia in central Ukraine. Situated near the village of Gavyryshivka, roughly 7-8 km southeast of the city center, it functions as an important hub for domestic flights and limited international connections. The airport has historically supported both civilian and military aviation activities typical of Ukrainian regional airfields.
faqs:
Q: What is the distance from Vinnytsia/Gavyryshivka Airport to the city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 7-8 kilometers southeast of central Vinnytsia, typically a 15-20 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Does Vinnytsia Airport offer international flights?
A: Yes, the airport handles a limited number of international routes, though its main focus has historically been on domestic Ukrainian connections.

Q: What facilities are available at VIN Airport?
A: The terminal provides standard regional airport amenities including a waiting hall, basic check-in counters, and parking areas, though services are more limited than at larger Ukrainian hubs like Boryspil.

Q: Is the airport operational year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates throughout the year, though flight schedules may be affected by seasonal demand and weather conditions common to central Ukraine.
transport_tips: Taxis and marshrutkas (shared minibuses) are the most common ways to reach the airport from Vinnytsia city center. Pre-arranging a taxi through a local service or hotel is recommended for early morning departures, as ride-hailing apps may have limited availability in the region.
local_tip: If you have a longer layover or early arrival, the nearby town of Vinnytsia itself is worth a quick visit—the famous Multimedia Fountain on the Southern Bug River is one of the largest floating fountains in Europe and is particularly impressive in the evening.
